info.title: Ambiguous Workspace API
info.description: Public REST API for the Ambiguous Workspace. Same surface every client uses — web, desktop, mobile, CLI, and AI agents. Authenticate with Authorization: Bearer <jwt-or-api-key>. REST API major version 1 is selected with the optional API-Version: 1 request header (the default). Responses echo API-Version. Unsupported versions return 400. Additive fields and endpoints may be introduced within a major version; incompatible changes require a new major version. Deprecated operations are marked deprecated in OpenAPI; a scheduled removal must advertise Deprecation and Sunset headers before removal. Rate-limited responses advertise RateLimit-Policy and RateLimit (remaining quota and reset seconds); 429 responses include Retry-After. Email sends accept Idempotency-Key for safe retries; consult the operation's header schema for its scope. A disposable task API sandbox is available at https://app.ambiguous.ai/sandbox with a separate contract at /sandbox/openapi.json and setup at https://ambiguous.ai/sandbox.md. It uses synthetic data and sandbox-only credentials; only its documented subset is supported.

api_key.description: Agent's API key (prefix `ak_…`). Shown exactly once — store it. Bearer-authenticate every subsequent request with this.

username.description: Auto-derived from `agent_display_name`; unique within the workspace.

workspace_email.description: The agent's inbound email address inside this workspace's domain.

agent.description: The newly-created agent user. Pair with `api_key` to make authenticated requests.

slug.description: The slug that actually got assigned — may differ from `workspace_slug` in the request if it was taken and the server auto-suggested an alternative.

provisional.description: Workspace starts provisional. Admin features (invites, billing, more-agent provisioning) are gated until a human claims via the emailed link.

workspace.description: The provisional workspace the agent is working in. Flips to provisional=false on successful claim.

email.description: Echo of `human_email` from the request.

claim_token_sent.description: True if the claim email was dispatched (SES returned a message ID). False on email-delivery failure — the token is still persisted and the URL can be handed to the human out of band. There is no account_id in the response: no account exists yet.

human.description: The pending human. Represented only by a claim token until they click the emailed link.

paired.description: True when the waiting browser was bound and will continue on its own. False when it was not — the signup still succeeded; only the browser hand-off was lost, and the human finishes through the emailed link instead.

reason.description: Why the browser was not bound: `pairing_expired` (the code lapsed), `pairing_not_found` (the code names no browser), or `pairing_completion_failed` (the signup landed but the pairing record did not). Null when `paired`.

browser_pairing.description: Present only when the request carried `browser_session`. A pairing that could not bind never refuses the signup — the rendezvous only decides whether one browser tab auto-advances — so callers read this rather than a non-2xx to learn the browser will not continue. The exception is a code that already bound a different signup, which still returns 409 so a retried command cannot mint a second workspace.

agent_display_name.description: Human-readable name for the agent (e.g. 'Research Bot'). Shown across the workspace UI and in outbound email From: headers.

human_email.description: Email of the human accountable for this agent. Receives a claim-token email with two CTAs: claim (become owner of the provisional workspace) or merge (move this agent into an existing workspace they run). No human account is created at signup — the claim token IS the human's representation until they click the link.

workspace_name.description: Display name for the new workspace. Defaults to `{agent_display_name}'s Workspace`.

workspace_slug.description: Requested URL slug. If omitted, the server derives one from `workspace_name` (kebab-cased), falling back to `{agent_display_name}-workspace` when no name is given or the name can't form a valid slug. If the derived or requested slug is taken, the server picks the first available suggestion from suggestAlternativeSlugs() and returns it in the response.

browser_session.description: Optional, short-lived browser pairing code. It signals the waiting marketing browser after signup; existing clients omit it.

reserved_local_parts.description: Merge only, and empty on a claim: every role address the merge carried and what happened to it, so a rename is never silent.

WorkspaceRole.description: Role granted to the user inside their current workspace. Drives permission gates across modules.

status.description: Lifecycle state. `pending` = awaiting action; `used` = already claimed or merged; `invalid` = unknown token.

workspace.description: The provisional workspace the token unlocks. Null for `invalid`.

agent_display_name.description: Display name of the agent in the provisional workspace. Null for `invalid`.

human_email.description: The email the token was sent to. Null for `invalid`.

human_has_account.description: True if `human_email` already has an account. Lets the claim page render a sign-in CTA (vs a password-create form) for the claim branch, and lets it render the merge option (requires an existing account with workspaces). Always false for `invalid`.

reserved_local_parts.description: Names in the provisional workspace that are role addresses of whatever workspace they end up in (postmaster@, support@). The claiming human is the first — and, on a merge, the only — admin this name will ever be in front of, so the page asks before the merge rather than reporting after it. Empty for an ordinary claim and for `used`/`invalid`.

username.description: The local-part the provisional workspace holds.

tier.description: `hard` is renamed at the merge whatever anyone says — RFC 2142 requires these to reach a human. `admin_overridable` is the claiming human's call: they are the target workspace's admin, and an admin deliberately granting `support@` is what the provisioning guard allows.

token.description: Session JWT — the claimant is now signed into the claimed workspace as `owner`.

workspace.description: The workspace the claim flipped from provisional to owned. Reflects any `workspace_name` / `workspace_slug` rename applied during claim.

user.description: The human's new user row inside the claimed workspace.

code.description: `slug_taken` when the requested `workspace_slug` is already in use. Absent for token-already-used.

suggestions.description: Available alternative slugs when `code = slug_taken`. Empty array if none could be generated.

AppleSignInResponse.description: Same session branches as Google sign-in: new account, MFA challenge, workspace picker, or authenticated.

registration_token.description: Same shape as the password-flow `/register` ready-response: short-lived JWT for workspace setup.

email.description: Echo of the Google-verified email (lowercased).

display_name.description: Display name from the Google profile.

needs_workspace_setup.description: Always true on this branch. Frontend should navigate to `/setup-workspace`.

kind.description: Discriminator. `mfa_required`: send a code to `/api/auth/mfa/verify`. `mfa_enrollment_required`: a workspace this sign-in lands in requires two-step verification, so set it up via `/api/auth/mfa/enroll/start` then `/confirm`.

mfa_token.description: Single-use sign-in challenge. Expires after 5 minutes or 5 attempts.

kind.description: Discriminator. Frontend should render the workspace-picker UI.

account_id.description: Account ID. Pass back via `/select-workspace` along with the chosen `workspace_id`.

workspaces.description: Opaque membership IDs and roles for every workspace this account belongs to. Names and slugs require the picker session token at `/picker-workspaces`, preventing pre-auth inventory disclosure.

picker_session_token.description: Short-lived JWT (5-min TTL, audience: workspace_picker) that authenticates the `/select-workspace` call. Pass as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` or in the request body.

id.description: Workspace ID. Pass back as `workspace_id` to `/select-workspace`.

role.description: Role this account holds inside the workspace.

account_id.description: Stable account ID for the authenticated human. Null only for agent principals.

workspace_id.description: Workspace scope carried by the returned JWT. Null only while workspace setup is still required.

user_id.description: Resolved `users.id` for the chosen account×workspace pair.

login_email.description: Account-level login email used to label locally saved human sessions. Null for agents.

primary_email.description: Best primary email for this user (workspace email > custom email > login email).

username.description: Derived workspace local-part (e.g. `phil` if workspace_email is `phil@acme.ambi.cc`).

allOf.description: Role in the workspace scope carried by the returned JWT.

token.description: Authentication JWT. Pass via `Authorization: Bearer <token>` for all subsequent API calls.

workspace_email.description: Computed workspace email or null. Present on `/login` + `/reset-password`; omitted on `/select-workspace`, `/google`, and `/apple` (single-workspace branch).

needs_workspace_setup.description: Present + true when the account has no workspace yet (frontend should redirect to `/setup-workspace`). Omitted otherwise.

consent_required.description: Present when the account must accept the current Terms and Privacy Policy before continuing.

RegisterResponse.description: Branch A returns when `REQUIRE_EMAIL_VERIFICATION=true`. Branch B returns when verification is disabled or the account is already verified (re-registration before workspace setup).

account_id.description: Newly-created account ID. Use this to call `/resend-verification` if the user never receives the email.

email.description: Echo of the registered email.

display_name.description: Echo of the registered display name.

message.description: User-facing message to render in the verify-email-pending screen.

email_verification_required.description: Always true on this branch. Frontend should redirect to `/verify-email-pending`.

registration_token.description: Short-lived JWT (`type: 'registration'`) that the workspace-creation endpoint exchanges for a workspace + a real auth JWT. See `POST /api/workspaces`.

email.description: Echo of the registered email.

display_name.description: Echo of the registered display name.

needs_workspace_setup.description: Always true on this branch. Frontend should navigate to `/setup-workspace`.

EntityReferenceMap.description: Entities referenced by `@{type:id}` tokens in this response, resolved under the requesting principal.

entity.description: Per-module preview row for the referenced entity.

captcha_required.description: Whether `POST /api/auth/register` requires a Turnstile `captcha_token` on this deployment.

captcha_site_key.description: Public Turnstile site key to render the check with; null when this deployment has none.

captcha_action.description: Turnstile `action` the token must be minted for.

target_workspace.description: The workspace the agent was merged into.

username.description: Possibly renamed from the provisional workspace's username if it collided with a user already in the target.

agent.description: The merged agent's user record in the target workspace. Its existing API key still works.

requested.description: The local-part the provisional workspace held.

assigned.description: What it holds in the target — equal to `requested` when kept.

reserved_local_parts.description: Every role address the merge carried across and what happened to it. Empty on an ordinary merge. Reported rather than logged because a rename changes an address the agent may already have given out.

mfa_recovery_regeneration_required.description: Present + true when a recovery code was used: generate a new set before continuing.
Present + true when a recovery code was used: generate a new set before continuing.

MfaVerifyResponse.description: The sign-in the challenge held: a workspace picker or an authenticated session.

secret.description: Base32 TOTP secret, for manual entry into an authenticator app.

otpauth_uri.description: `otpauth://totp/...` URI for a QR code or a direct link.

recovery_codes.description: Ten single-use recovery codes. Shown once and never retrievable again.
Ten single-use recovery codes. Shown once and never retrievable again.

MfaEnrollConfirmResponse.description: The completed sign-in plus the new recovery codes.

GoogleSignInResponse.description: Four branches: brand-new account → registration_token; existing account holding a second factor, or entering a workspace that requires one → MFA challenge; existing account in multiple workspaces → picker; existing account in 0 or 1 workspaces → authenticated.

LoginResponse.description: An MFA challenge (the account holds a second factor, or its only workspace requires one), a workspace picker (multi-workspace account), or authenticated (single workspace, or no workspace yet → `needs_workspace_setup: true`).

account_id.description: Account ID. Pass to `/resend-verification` if the user lost the email.

SelectWorkspaceResponse.description: Authenticated, or an MFA enrolment challenge when the chosen workspace requires two-step verification and the account has none.

registration_token.description: Short-lived JWT. Use `POST /api/workspaces` with this token to create the user's first workspace.

email.description: Verified email.

display_name.description: Display name from the account record.

needs_workspace_setup.description: True when the account holds no workspace membership yet — frontend navigates to `/setup-workspace`. False when it already belongs to a workspace, in which case the frontend continues to sign-in; a verification link is not a session credential.

already_verified.description: True when the email was already verified. Idempotent double-click returns 200 instead of 400.

phone_last4.description: Last 4 digits of the verified phone number — safe to render in UI.

ResetPasswordResponse.description: Auto-login after a successful reset: same response shape as `/login`. Workspace_picker branch fires for multi-workspace accounts.

consent_version.description: The TOS version the user has now consented to.

email.description: The email that was just verified.

code.description: One-time UUID code. Single-use; expires 60s after creation. Trade at POST /api/auth/native/exchange.

email.description: Backward-compat alias for `primary_email`.

instructions.description: Copy-ready connection prompt for the API key's principal.

CliLoginResponse.description: Discriminated by `port` + `state` presence: provided → redirect; omitted → direct token.

redirect.description: URL of the form `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback?code=<one-time-code>&state=<state>`. The CLI's local server captures this, then exchanges the code via `/cli/exchange`.

token.description: Authentication JWT (only returned when `port` + `state` are NOT provided).

email.description: Backward-compat alias for `primary_email` for old CLI versions.

allOf.description: Account kind. Humans authenticate with email+password or a supported SSO provider; agents authenticate with API keys.

workspace_email.description: Computed in-workspace email (`<username>@<default-workspace-domain>`). A verified custom domain is used only after an Admin selects it as the workspace default. Null when the user has no username or the workspace can't be resolved. Pickers showing in-workspace identity should prefer this over `primary_email` (which can be a personal external email).

WorkspaceUserSummary.description: Public-ish user record returned by the workspace `users` listing — no role, no external emails, no preferences. Powers assignee/mention pickers across modules.

harness.description: The agent runtime the click came from (`claude-code`, `openclaw`, …), or null when no click identified one or it named one we ship no panel for. Null is the ordinary case, because the step opens for every signup — a marketing arrival is what supplies a label, not what opens the step. Selects which connect instructions open by default; never echoed as raw input.

declined.description: True once the person pressed **Skip for now**. The decline is durable — nothing re-opens the step on its own again — but it does not spend the account's one provision, which is why this object stays non-null: the account is still eligible to complete the step from the Home checklist.

id.description: `users.id` of the agent this step provisioned.

workspace_email.description: The agent's inbound address inside this workspace's domain.

provisioned_agent.description: Non-null once the step has provisioned its agent and the person has not yet pressed **Continue** on the Agent-ready screen. The key is shown once and never re-sent, so a client reaching this state renders the screen for this agent with a mint-a-new-key affordance instead of the spent key. Null before provisioning; the whole object goes null on acknowledgement.

account_id.description: Stable account ID. Null only for agent principals.

id.description: User row ID — `users.id` for this account×workspace pair.

allOf.description: Account kind. Humans authenticate with email+password or a supported SSO provider; agents authenticate with API keys.

primary_email.description: Best primary email (workspace email > custom email > login email).

login_email.description: Account-level login email. Null for agents.

email_verified.description: Whether the account's login email is verified (`accounts.email_verified`). Null for agents and workspace rows with no account.

has_password.description: Whether the account has a sign-in password set. False for SSO-only accounts, which can set one through the password-reset flow. Null for agents and workspace rows with no account.

workspace_id.description: Active workspace ID. Null when the account has no workspace yet (`needs_workspace_setup: true`).

workspace_name.description: Active workspace name. Null when the account has no workspace yet.

workspace_email.description: Derived workspace email. Null when the workspace has no email domain configured.

username.description: Workspace-derived username (local-part of the workspace email).

custom_email.description: Verified custom-domain email used as the From: address when the user picks 'send as custom'.

default_send_as.description: ID of the alias selected as the default `Send as` address when composing email.

email_signature.description: Personal email signature, appended to outbound mail.

meeting_url.description: Personal meeting URL (Zoom, Google Meet, etc.) used by /meet slash command.

avatar_url.description: Proxy URL (`/api/users/:id/avatar?v=…`) or null. See D071 for why this is a proxy URL, not a presigned GCS URL.

has_seen_welcome_modal.description: Onboarding flag. Frontend uses this to decide whether to show the first-run modal.

has_dismissed_onboarding.description: True when the user has permanently dismissed the Get Started onboarding checklist.

analytics_opt_out.description: True when the user has opted out of non-essential analytics and data processing (Art. 21 GDPR).

allOf.description: Role in the active workspace.

kind.description: `coworker` runs the first-party engine; `agent` is a third-party identity.

manager.description: The human accountable for this agent. Null when unassigned.

agent.description: Agent-specific identity context. Null for human principals.

is_internal_admin.description: True when the account's login email is in INTERNAL_ADMIN_EMAILS — gates internal-staff surfaces (the architecture / agents-modules docs sites, /internal/*). Distinct from the workspace `role`; always false for agents.

can_provision_coworkers.description: True when this account may provision coworkers (POST /api/coworkers/provision) — internal team, or any caller while COWORKER_PROVISIONING_OPEN. Pre-GA gate; drives the Coworker option in the New agent dialog.

primary_external_email_id.description: If set, points at a verified `user_external_emails` row whose email becomes `primary_email`. Null → workspace email is primary.

needs_workspace_setup.description: True when `workspace_id` is null. Frontend should redirect to `/setup-workspace`.

pending_agent_onboarding.description: Non-null while this account has not yet spent its one guided create-agent provision. The step opens for EVERY workspace signup, not only for one that carried `intent=invite-agent` — that intent supplies `harness` and nothing else. Read `declined` to tell an untouched step (open `/invite-agent` rather than landing the person on an empty workspace) from a skipped one (do not redirect; the Home checklist is its door). Stays non-null after provisioning, carrying `provisioned_agent`, until `POST /api/identity/onboarding-agent/acknowledge` records that the person left the Agent-ready screen — so a reload lands back on it rather than on an empty workspace with the key unread. Goes null on acknowledgement and cannot re-open after.

created_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when the user record was created. Used by the frontend to guard time-sensitive onboarding modals (D-GROUPS-067).

ws_trace.description: True when the active workspace is in WS_TRACE_WORKSPACE_IDS — gates the client realtime delivery-trace beacon (`ws.received`). Default false; the trace is inert for every unflagged workspace.

allOf.description: Account kind. Humans authenticate with email+password or a supported SSO provider; agents authenticate with API keys.

UserSummary.description: Compact profile shape returned by `/send-as`, `/avatar` upload, and `/avatar` delete. Excludes workspace + role + external-email fields.

file.description: The avatar image (multipart `file` field): JPEG, PNG, GIF, or WebP, at most 5MB.

enabled.description: Whether the account has a confirmed authenticator.

confirmed_at.description: When the current authenticator was confirmed.

recovery_regeneration_required.description: True after a recovery code was used, until a new set is generated.

required_by_workspace.description: True when a workspace this account belongs to requires two-step verification, so it cannot be turned off.

recovery_codes.description: Ten single-use recovery codes. Shown once and never retrievable again.

token.description: A new session token. Every other session for the account was signed out.

email.description: Verified or unverified email address.

verified.description: True after the user clicks the verification link.

is_login_email.description: True for the row that mirrors the account's login email (read-only — cannot be removed).

email_on_comment_added.description: Send transactional email when someone comments on a doc/task/etc. owned by this user. Default: true.

email_on_mention.description: Send email when this user is @mentioned in a comment or message. Default: true.

email_on_task_assigned.description: Send email when a task is assigned to this user. Default: true.

email_on_document_shared.description: Send email when a document, sheet, slide, wiki page, file, or calendar is shared with this user. Default: true.

email_on_deal_won.description: Send email when a deal owned by this user is marked won. Default: true.

email_on_deal_lost.description: Send email when a deal owned by this user is marked lost. Default: true.

sound_on_new_notification.description: Client-only UX cue. Play a chime when a new notification arrives in this browser tab. Default: false.

browser_push_on_new_notification.description: Client-only UX cue. Show an OS-level browser push notification. Default: false.

tab_title_unread_count.description: Client-only UX cue. Update the tab title with `(N) Ambiguous` when the tab has unread notifications. Default: false.

NotificationPreferences.description: Per-user email + arrival-cue gating. Email keys default true (fail-open); arrival cues default false. Per-event browser push lives in the unified notification-settings surface (GET/PUT /api/users/:id/notifications).

owner_username.description: Owner's username (slug-form). Populated for both human and agent owners; null only when owner row has no username.

content.description: Authoring format. Docs use ProseMirror JSON; sheets/slides use JSON canvas. May be null on freshly-created entities.

import_warnings.description: Content the conversion could not represent, one string per drop. A tag with no schema mapping is kept as literal text and is not a drop; this reports styling, decorative wrappers and head-only elements. Present on every `type: doc` create and update, empty when nothing was dropped. Absent for sheets and slides, and for an editor-session save, which stores no converted body.

content.description: Document body. For type=doc, accepts Markdown (recommended) or a ProseMirror JSON string. HTML is tolerated best-effort: a tag the editor schema maps becomes its node or mark, so `x` stores `x` in bold. A tag it does not map is kept as literal text, attributes and closing tag verbatim, so `` survives a round trip. Styling and decorative wrappers are still dropped and are listed in `import_warnings` on the response. For type=sheet/slide, see the respective module's authoring format. To insert a native smart chip (the live-status chip the editor inserts), write `@{task:}` in Markdown; `doc`, `sheet`, `slide`, `canvas` and `wiki_page` ids work the same way, and the chip takes the entity's title when you can read it. Wrap a token in backticks to keep it as text.

role.description: The role the grant carries for the caller on this document.

SharedWithMeWorkspace.description: The workspace that shared this document. Not the caller's own workspace when the grant is external.

content.description: Replacement document body. For type=doc, accepts Markdown (recommended) or a ProseMirror JSON string. HTML is tolerated best-effort: a mapped tag becomes its node or mark, an unmapped tag is kept as literal text, and styling and decorative wrappers are dropped and listed in `import_warnings` on the response. To insert a native smart chip (the live-status chip the editor inserts), write `@{task:<task-uuid>}` in Markdown; `doc`, `sheet`, `slide`, `canvas` and `wiki_page` ids work the same way, and the chip takes the entity's title when you can read it. Wrap a token in backticks to keep it as text. Mutually exclusive with `operations`.

suggesting.description: Commenter-relaxed write: content changes must carry track-change marks (auto-wrapped for agents).

operations.description: Block-id-targeted edits as an alternative to `content` replacement. `content` field on each op is Markdown that is converted to PM JSON and applied at the matched blockId; `@{task:<task-uuid>}` becomes a native smart chip.

starred.description: Omit to toggle the current state.

workspace_email.description: Computed in-workspace address (`<username>@<default-workspace-domain>`). A verified custom domain is used only after an Admin selects it as the workspace default.

invite_type.description: Which outcome the sharer picked: `member` staged a workspace invite, `external_grant` a per-resource grant.

can_manage.description: Whether THIS caller may add, change or revoke a grant here right now — their rung with the owner's opt-out already applied, so a client never re-derives it.

editors_can_share.description: The owner's opt-out as stored. `false` means only the owner may share.

status.description: accepted means SES acknowledged the send, not recipient delivery or inbox placement. unconfirmed means no send acknowledgment; the invitation or grant still exists. Do not automatically retry an ambiguous send.

invite_to_workspace.description: Which of the two outcomes this recipient gets. Absent or `false` is an EXTERNAL GRANT: they reach this one resource and never become a member — no seat, no member-cap slot, and no row in any member list. It binds to one of the recipient's own identities with NO accept call: live on their next authenticated request when the address already resolves to a verified identity, and on first sign-in and verification otherwise (`specs/architecture/external-collaboration.md#grant-identity-binding`). `true` is a WORKSPACE INVITE: accepting adds them as a member, so that outcome does land on acceptance. An address that is an agent's workspace email is refused `400 invite_target_is_agent` on the `true` path — an agent joins a workspace only through provisioning — while the default path grants to that agent's own identity normally.

expires_at.description: ISO 8601 deadline for the grant, or null for no expiry. Bounded by the `shareExpiryMaxDays` platform limit.

workspace_role.description: The Everyone-team share role while visibility is `workspace`; null otherwise.

visibility.description:
One of the values in `VALID_VISIBILITY_VALUES`. What each one grants, measured against both read routes:

`restricted`: the owner and explicit shares only.

`workspace`: every member of the owning workspace, at `workspace_role`. A caller outside that workspace gets 404 on both routes.

`link` and `public`: identical in behaviour today. Both grant every workspace member a role, and both publish the document to two kinds of outside caller. A SIGNED-IN non-member reads it at `GET /api/documents/{id}` and holds `link_permission`. An ANONYMOUS caller reads it only at `GET /api/public/documents/{id}`.

`GET /api/documents/{id}` is never anonymous. It answers 401 with no credential whatever the visibility, because auth middleware runs before any visibility check. Setting `public` does not open that route to the world, and no visibility value does.

Both outside paths carry `X-Link-Password` on a gated link. The anonymous route answers 401 `password_required` without it and accepts a retry carrying the header; the signed-in non-member sends the same header on `GET /api/documents/{id}` and is admitted at `link_permission`, or gets 404 without it. Past `link_expires_at` BOTH answer 404 — an elapsed link is indistinguishable from an id that was never shared, and never reports expiry (`agents/INTERFACES.md` Pat8).

Handing a document to an agent in another workspace: if it can sign in, `public` or `link` plus `GET /api/documents/{id}` works. If it cannot, point it at `GET /api/public/documents/{id}` and leave `link_password` unset.

It binds to one of the recipient's own identities with NO accept call: live on their next authenticated request when the address already resolves to a verified identity, and on first sign-in and verification otherwise (`specs/architecture/external-collaboration.md#grant-identity-binding`). `true` is a WORKSPACE INVITE: accepting adds them as a member, so that outcome does land on acceptance. filters.description: Free-form filter JSON; structure matches the list query params.

TaskView.description: Saved task view (filter + layout). `is_shared: true` means visible to the whole workspace.

progress.description: Aggregate task counts by status, plus a 0-100 percentage of tasks completed.

TaskGoal.description: OKR-style goal entity. Tasks link to one goal via `tasks.goal_id`.

TaskGoalStatus.description: Lifecycle state of an OKR-style goal.

task_ids.description: Tasks to update. Both `task_ids` and `ids` are accepted by the route.

TaskBulkUpdateInput.description: Body of `POST /api/tasks/bulk/update`. Unknown keys are rejected — a mistyped field must fail closed, never silently no-op.

project_id.description: Clear completed tasks within this project.

all_projects.description: Explicit opt-in to clear completed tasks across ALL projects in the workspace. Destructive — must be `true` to clear workspace-wide; never the default.

count.description: Untriaged tasks assigned to the caller — the sidebar inbox badge.

triage_count.description: Always 0 at present. Reserved for the projects-in-triage half of the bucket, which is not counted yet.

worked_at.description: Date (YYYY-MM-DD) the work was performed, or null for timer-started entries.

user_name.description: Hydrated on list endpoints for display; omitted on single-entry returns.

TaskTimeEntry.description: Time tracking entry for a task. Open entries have `stopped_at: null`.

TaskActiveTimerResponse.description: Returns the user's currently-running timer, or `null` if none.

TaskFavorite.description: Sidebar favorite — pins a view or project for the current user.

TaskFavoriteRemoveInput.description: Body of `DELETE /api/tasks/favorites` — matched on resource_type + resource_id.

status_counts.description: Count per system status across the whole filter, not just this page.

custom_status_counts.description: Count per custom status id across the whole filter, not just this page.

blocked_task_ids.description: IDs of tasks in `data` whose dependencies are not all done.

archived_count.description: Count of archived tasks matching the filter (regardless of `showArchived`).

limit.description: Echo of the request `limit` (offset mode only).

offset.description: Echo of the request `offset` (offset mode only).

TaskListSort.description: Sort order for `GET /api/tasks`. `updated_at` (recently-touched first) is the default; `sort_order` for board / drag-reorder; `created_at` for chronology; `due_date` for deadline proximity; `priority` for urgency ranking.

title.description: Task title. Required. Max 255 chars; trimmed before insert.

description.description: Markdown body. Rendered with the standard task-card markdown subset.

status.description: Initial status. Defaults to `todo`. If `task_status_id` is also set, that takes precedence and `status` is overridden by the custom status's category.

assignee_id.description: User to assign the task to. Must be in the caller's workspace (403 otherwise). Omit for unassigned.

due_date.description: ISO 8601 date (YYYY-MM-DD). If unset and a `priority` is given, the SLA policy auto-sets a due date and stamps `due_date_source: 'sla'`.

start_date.description: ISO 8601 date (YYYY-MM-DD); with `due_date` defines a date range.

parent_task_id.description: Parent task for subtasks. Omit for top-level tasks.

contact_id.description: Link the task to a CRM contact; auto-logs a CRM activity row.

deal_id.description: Link the task to a CRM deal.

recurrence_rule.description: RFC 5545 RRULE string. When set, completing the task spawns the next occurrence.

goal_id.description: Link the task to an OKR-style goal.

cycle_id.description: Sprint/cycle this task is scheduled in.

label_ids.description: Labels to assign at create time. Each ID must reference a label in the caller's workspace (404 otherwise).

subscriber_ids.description: Users to subscribe to the task at create time so they receive update notifications. Each must be a member of the caller's workspace; IDs outside the workspace are silently skipped. Use to link a bug reporter to the filed task.

TaskCreateInput.description: Body of `POST /api/tasks`. Captures the union of fields any surface accepts.

TaskSubscription.description: Subscription entry for a task — drives notification fan-out.

user_id.description: Subscribe another user who has access to the task. Omit (send `{}`) to subscribe the caller.

removed.description: True when a subscription was removed, false when there was none to remove. Without it a removal and a no-op are identical on the wire, and the caller has to re-read the subscriber list to tell them apart.

TaskCollaborator.description: A collaborator on one task — holds `editor` on it and its subtasks, never on its project (TASKS P3).

user_id.description: The workspace member to share this task with. Subscribed on add.

TaskPrLink.description: Pull request linked to a task via the integration-links service.

TaskComment.description: Threaded task comment. Top-level comments have `parent_id: null` and carry their replies inline; reply comments carry an empty `replies` array.

TaskCommentAuthor.description: Comment author summary. `primary_email` is the user's verified primary email (may be null for legacy accounts that haven't re-verified).

content.description: Markdown body. Min 1 char after trim.

parent_id.description: Parent comment ID for replies. Omit for top-level comments.

idempotency_key.description: Stable key for retry-safe comment creation. Reusing it returns the original comment.

duration_minutes.description: Duration in minutes. Manual entries only — timer auto-fills this on stop.

worked_at.description: ISO 8601 date (YYYY-MM-DD) the work was performed. Defaults to today when omitted.

TaskActivityEntry.description: One audit-log row for a task (status change, assignment, comment, etc.).

type.description: 'related' | 'blocking' | 'blocked_by' | 'duplicate'

TaskRelation.description: Edge in the task-relations graph. `blocking`/`blocked_by` pairs are auto-mirrored.

mark_as_duplicate.description: When `type=duplicate`: also cancel the source task and add a system comment.

due_date_source.description: Defaults to `manual` when `due_date` changes through this update. Set explicitly to `sla` to mark a system-set due date.

time_spent_minutes.description: Manual override; usually auto-managed by time entries.

subscriber_ids.description: Users to subscribe to this task so they receive update notifications. Additive — existing subscribers are untouched. Each must be a workspace member; IDs outside the workspace are silently skipped. Use to backfill a bug reporter onto an existing task.

TaskUpdateInput.description: Body of `PATCH /api/tasks/:id`. All fields optional; `null` clears nullable fields.

config.description: Template payload — initial milestones, default tasks, member roles.

workspace_id.description: `projects.workspace_id` is a nullable FK; a row predating workspace stamping carries none.

ProjectStatus.description: Latest status update on the project. `null` when no updates have been posted.

total.description: Tasks in the project, every status included.

percentage.description: done / (todo + in_progress + done), rounded. Cancelled tasks are excluded from the denominator.

task_percentage.description: Task completion across the project's milestones, rounded — the figure the sidebar bar renders when milestones exist.

type.description: Which principal this grant names. The workspace tier is the Everyone team's row, so a project's access list carries team rows alongside user rows.

workspace_email.description: Computed in-workspace address (`<username>@<default-workspace-domain>`). A verified custom domain is used only after an Admin selects it as the workspace default.

body.description: `null` when the update carries a status change and no prose — the column is nullable and the handler has nothing to substitute.

workspace_email.description: Computed in-workspace address (`<username>@<default-workspace-domain>`). A verified custom domain is used only after an Admin selects it as the workspace default.

avatar_url.description: The author's avatar image. Null when none is set.

CycleVelocity.description: Recent completed cycles, most recent first.

SheetSummary.description: Lightweight sheet metadata returned in list responses. Does NOT carry the structured `data` body — call GET /api/sheets/:id to load the full sheet.

SheetListResponse.description: List of sheets accessible to the caller (owned + shared), filtered to `type: sheet`. Mirrors the `/api/documents` list envelope but without rendering doc or slide rows.

sheets.description: The wire key the server actually returns the tab list under (same element shape as `tabs`).

conditionalFormats.description: The key the conditional-format endpoints read and write.

conditionalFormatRules.description: Import-accepted alias for `conditionalFormats` (`WORKBOOK_FIELDS`); never written by this API.

SheetData.description: JSON canvas — the structured sheet body (tabs, columns, rows, formulas). Returned nested under `data` on the `Sheet` envelope; never returned at the response root.

SheetRow.description: Row keyed by column id → cell value.

SheetCellValue.description: Cell value. `null` = empty. Formulas are stored as `=...` strings.

ranges.description: All A1-style areas when one native rule targets a multi-area range.

ValidationRuleType.description: Mirror of Google Sheets API v4 validation rule types.

ConnectorConfig.description: Provider-specific connection settings; shape depends on `type`.

ConnectorStatus.description: Outcome of the connector's most recent run. `error` is what SHEETS.md E14 fans out on.

can_edit.description: True when the caller has editor or owner role on this sheet.

Sheet.description: Envelope response shape returned by every Sheet GET/POST/PATCH endpoint. Top-level fields carry document metadata (id, title, owner, visibility, timestamps); the structured sheet body — tabs, columns, rows, formulas — is nested under `data` (see `SheetData`). SDK consumers must read cells/columns/tabs as `response.data.tabs[…]`, not at the response root.

title.description: Optional title. Defaults to 'Untitled' when omitted.

content.description: Optional initial SheetData (JSON canvas). String is parsed as JSON server-side; object is stringified.

updatedRange.description: A1 range the append actually wrote, e.g. `Sheet1!A4:C6`.

values.description: 2-D array of row × column values. Capped at 1000 rows per call.

ranges.description: Array of A1-style range specs. Capped at 100 per call.

sheetName.description: Name the copied tab landed under in the destination spreadsheet.

index.description: Zero-based position of the copied tab in the destination's tab list.

SheetRangeCellValue.description: A cell value as a range read returns it: the stored scalar, or — on `valueRenderOption=EVALUATED` — one of the two rendered-element sentinels.

ImageCellValue.description: IMAGE() result — the grid renders an rather than text.

LinkCellValue.description: HYPERLINK() result — the grid renders an <a> rather than text.

sheet.description: Tab the cell was written to; absent when the update carried no per-row tab.

updatedCells.description: Present only when `includeValuesInResponse=true`: the value each updated cell holds after the write.

SheetWithUpdatedCells.description: Envelope response shape returned by every Sheet GET/POST/PATCH endpoint. Top-level fields carry document metadata (id, title, owner, visibility, timestamps); the structured sheet body — tabs, columns, rows, formulas — is nested under `data` (see `SheetData`). SDK consumers must read cells/columns/tabs as `response.data.tabs[…]`, not at the response root.

cells.description: Alias for `updates` — accepted by the API client.

pivotTables.description: Every pivot table across every tab, each annotated with the tab name it lives in.

charts.description: Every chart across every tab, each annotated with the tab name it lives in.

tab.description: Tab name where the chart lives. Defaults to the first tab.

columnId.description: Column id within the source range that this slicer filters.

selectedValues.description: null = pass-through ('All'); [] = filter out everything ('None'); non-empty array = only these values pass.

slicers.description: Every slicer across every tab, each annotated with the tab name it lives in.

tab.description: Tab name where the slicer lives. Defaults to the first tab.

height.description: Canvas height in slide-units (e.g. 540 for 16:9, 720 for 4:3).

colorUserSet.description: True when the user picked `color` explicitly; theme application preserves user-set colors instead of remapping them.

delay.description: Delay before the animation starts, in milliseconds.

order.description: Sequencing index among animations on the same slide.

RichTextContent.description: ProseMirror JSON for per-character rich text. Stamped onto every text element on read, so it is present on the wire even when the deck was authored without it.

allOf.description: ProseMirror JSON for rich text inside the shape. Stamped on read, like the text element's.

duration_s.description: Transition duration in seconds (float, 0.1–10). Canonical field.

speed.description: Legacy preset (slow=1.0s, medium=0.5s, fast=0.3s) — normalized to duration_s on write.

SlideDeckData.description: JSON canvas — the structured deck body (settings, slides, master slides). Returned nested under `data` on the `SlideDeck` envelope; never returned at the response root.

can_edit.description: True when the caller has editor or owner role on this deck (can mutate slides, settings, masters). False for viewer/commenter callers — clients use this to gate the editor toolbar, drag/resize handles, and write-path UI.

SlideDeck.description: Envelope response shape returned by every Slides GET/POST/PATCH endpoint. Top-level fields carry document metadata (id, title, slide_count, owner, visibility, timestamps, can_edit); the structured deck body — settings, slides, master slides — is nested under `data` (see `SlideDeckData`). SDK consumers must read settings/slides as `response.data.slides[…]`, not at the response root.

title.description: Title for the new deck. Defaults to 'Untitled' if omitted.

slide.description: Slide body (full or partial — service merges).

elements.description: Element list. Convenience for callers that don't wrap in `slide`.
Full-replace element list for the slide.

slide.description: Alternative envelope — fields merged with top-level keys.

allOf.description: The group element just created, spread beside the deck.

SlideDeckWithGroup.description: Envelope response shape returned by every Slides GET/POST/PATCH endpoint. Top-level fields carry document metadata (id, title, slide_count, owner, visibility, timestamps, can_edit); the structured deck body — settings, slides, master slides — is nested under `data` (see `SlideDeckData`). SDK consumers must read settings/slides as `response.data.slides[…]`, not at the response root.

element_ids.description: Element IDs to group on the slide.

promoted_elements.description: The elements lifted out of the dissolved group, now top-level on the slide.

SlideDeckWithPromotedElements.description: Envelope response shape returned by every Slides GET/POST/PATCH endpoint. Top-level fields carry document metadata (id, title, slide_count, owner, visibility, timestamps, can_edit); the structured deck body — settings, slides, master slides — is nested under `data` (see `SlideDeckData`). SDK consumers must read settings/slides as `response.data.slides[…]`, not at the response root.

allOf.description: The newly created copy.

SlideDeckWithDuplicatedSlide.description: Envelope response shape returned by every Slides GET/POST/PATCH endpoint. Top-level fields carry document metadata (id, title, slide_count, owner, visibility, timestamps, can_edit); the structured deck body — settings, slides, master slides — is nested under `data` (see `SlideDeckData`). SDK consumers must read settings/slides as `response.data.slides[…]`, not at the response root.

duration_s.description: Transition duration in seconds (float, 0.1–10). Preferred over speed/duration.

speed.description: Legacy preset — normalized to duration_s (slow=1.0, medium=0.5, fast=0.3).

duration.description: Legacy duration in ms — normalized to duration_s (duration/1000, clamped 0.1–10).

transition.description: Transition applied to every slide. Provide duration_s (seconds, preferred), speed (legacy preset), or duration (legacy ms).

order.description: New slide order — array of original indices in the desired sequence.

defaultBackground.description: Camel-case alias accepted by the SDK.

showSlideNumbers.description: Camel-case alias accepted by the SDK (AMB-6729).

SlideDeckWithOccurrences.description: Envelope response shape returned by every Slides GET/POST/PATCH endpoint. Top-level fields carry document metadata (id, title, slide_count, owner, visibility, timestamps, can_edit); the structured deck body — settings, slides, master slides — is nested under `data` (see `SlideDeckData`). SDK consumers must read settings/slides as `response.data.slides[…]`, not at the response root.

SlideDeckWithFontCounts.description: Envelope response shape returned by every Slides GET/POST/PATCH endpoint. Top-level fields carry document metadata (id, title, slide_count, owner, visibility, timestamps, can_edit); the structured deck body — settings, slides, master slides — is nested under `data` (see `SlideDeckData`). SDK consumers must read settings/slides as `response.data.slides[…]`, not at the response root.

heading.description: Font for headings and titles — text at 28px or larger.

body.description: Font for body text — text below 28px, and every table.

SlideDeckWithReplacements.description: Envelope response shape returned by every Slides GET/POST/PATCH endpoint. Top-level fields carry document metadata (id, title, slide_count, owner, visibility, timestamps, can_edit); the structured deck body — settings, slides, master slides — is nested under `data` (see `SlideDeckData`). SDK consumers must read settings/slides as `response.data.slides[…]`, not at the response root.

template_id.description: ID of the template to apply (e.g. `business-pitch`).

scope.description: `all` repaints the entire deck with the template; `current_slide` replaces just one slide with the template's first slide.

current_slide_index.description: Required when `scope = current_slide`. Zero-based index of the slide to replace.

placeholders.description: Map of `{{key}}` → value substitutions. Unknown keys are left literal so the user can spot them.

locked.description: A locked element rejects geometry/content mutation until unlocked.

frameId.description: Owning frame id when the element lives inside a frame.

groupId.description: Group membership; elements sharing a groupId move/rotate/delete as a unit.

Absent or `false` is an EXTERNAL GRANT: they reach this one resource and never become a member — no seat, no member-cap slot, and no row in any member list.
