revoked_count.description: How many grants in this workspace were removed. Every one they held, so this is the blast radius of the action just taken.

raw_key.description: Plaintext API key. Only returned at create time.

old_key_expires_at.description: ISO timestamp when the previous key stops working (rotate only).

user_id.description: Workspace user the key is minted for. Required.

SubscriptionStatus.description: Stripe subscription status, mirrored on our row.

DomainStatusRead.description: Domain provisioning state. Current vocabulary: see DomainStatus. The underlying column is unconstrained text, so a caller must tolerate a value outside it.

name.description: Active workspace name. Falls back to `Ambiguous` if the JWT has no workspaceId or the workspace row is missing.

slug.description: Active workspace slug. Falls back to `ambiguous` when the workspace row is missing.

logo_url.description: Workspace logo URL stored in `workspace_settings.workspace_logo_url`. Null when unset.

error.description: Always `Workspace name has already been customized. Pass { force: true } to overwrite.`.

current_name.description: The current customized workspace name. UI surfaces this so the user can confirm overwrite.

CheckSlugResponse.description: Availability decision. Always returns 200 — even malformed/reserved/taken slugs surface as `available: false` with an error message. The 400 status is only used when the `slug` query parameter is missing entirely.

available.description: Slug is well-formed AND not taken AND not reserved.
Slug is taken, reserved, or malformed.

error.description: Human-readable reason. Stable substrings the UI matches against include 'at least 3', 'at most 48', 'lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens', 'consecutive', 'hyphen', 'reserved', 'taken'.

code.description: Machine-readable reason (e.g. `slug_too_short`, `slug_reserved`, `slug_taken`) so a caller branches on a stable token rather than matching `error` prose. Absent on the missing-parameter 400.

suggestions.description: Available alternative slugs (e.g. `acme-2`, `acme-team`). Only present when the slug was rejected because it's taken — not for reserved or malformed inputs.

role.description: Role this account holds in the workspace (`owner`, `admin`, `member`, `guest`, or a custom role name).

workspace_email.description: Reserved for the derived workspace email — currently always null at this endpoint.

joined_at.description: ISO timestamp the user joined this workspace (`users.created_at`). Null on legacy rows pre-onboarding.

is_active.description: True for the workspace this JWT currently scopes to. Exactly one row has this flag set per response.

data.description: All workspaces the authenticated account belongs to, ordered by `joined_at` ascending.

has_more.description: Always false. Workspace memberships per account are bounded; pagination is not currently implemented.

active_workspace_id.description: ID of the currently-active workspace from the JWT. Matches exactly one `data[*].id` (or null if the user somehow has no active workspace).

restored.description: True when the workspace is no longer archived.

harness.description: The agent runtime the journey came from, or null when none was identified — the ordinary case, since the step opens for every signup rather than only for a marketing arrival. Selects which connect instructions the flow opens with.

CreatedWorkspaceAgentOnboarding.description: Present whenever this account has not yet spent its one guided create-agent provision — which is every fresh account, not only one that signed up through `intent=invite-agent`. **It carries no agent and no key** — nothing is provisioned here. It is the signal to open `/invite-agent` before `/invite-team`, so the person is guided rather than dropped on an empty workspace. Absent once the step has been completed.

user_id.description: `users.id` of the founding user row inside the new workspace.

username.description: Workspace email local-part (e.g. `ryan`). Null when no email domain is configured for the workspace.

workspace_email.description: Founder's derived workspace email (`{username}@{domain}`).

token.description: Fresh JWT scoped to the new workspace. Replaces the registration_token (which is single-use).
Fresh JWT carrying the target workspace ID. Use as the `Authorization: Bearer` for all subsequent requests.

header_names.description: Names of the custom request headers sent on every delivery. Values are write-only and never returned.

secret.description: HMAC signing secret. Only returned at creation time.

previous_secret_expires_at.description: ISO-8601. Old secret remains valid until this timestamp (24h grace).

url.description: Generated image as a `data:` URL (base64-encoded). Embed directly into Docs/Slides without a separate Drive upload step.

email.description: Email address, or null.

phone.description: Phone in the format printed on the card, or null.

address.description: Physical address joined into one line, or null.

notes.description: Anything else printed on the card — social handles, fax, secondary phone, tagline. Null when nothing extra is present.

text.description: The cleaned transcript. Whisper artifacts (`[silence]`, `(inaudible)`, the silence-fallback `you`) are stripped before return; an empty-speech response surfaces as 422 `No speech detected` instead of an empty string here.

duration.description: Audio duration in seconds, as reported by Whisper's `verbose_json` response. Used by the metering middleware to compute `ceil(duration / 60)` minutes for the per-minute action debit.

language.description: Whisper's detected language (full English name, e.g. `english`, `spanish`). Absent when `language` was supplied on the request.

audio.description: Audio file to transcribe. Accepted formats: mp3, mp4, mpeg, mpga, m4a, wav, webm. Max 25 MB. Whisper hard-cap of 15 minutes per request applies (anti-abuse — files > 15 min return 413).

language.description: ISO-639-1 language code (e.g. `en`, `es`, `fr`). When provided, Whisper skips automatic detection and decodes against the named language — improves accuracy for short clips or accented speech.

prompt.description: Optional decoder priming string. Whisper biases the transcript toward vocabulary in this string (proper nouns, jargon). Max 224 tokens — anything beyond is silently truncated upstream.

approvals.description: Pending email approvals for agents the caller is the manager of. Admin authority alone never counts.

public_key.description: VAPID public key (base64url, uncompressed P-256). Pass to `PushManager.subscribe({applicationServerKey})`.

subprotocol.description: The `cap-v1-<compact-JWS>` value to present as the WebSocket subprotocol on the next /ws/mux upgrade. Opaque to the client: never parsed, never logged, never persisted to disk (#realtime-edge-security-privacy).

expires_at.description: Expiry, integer seconds since the Unix epoch. The client refreshes inside a randomized window before this instant; expiry is enforced by the edge even if a refresh never arrives.

lifetime_seconds.description: Seconds this capability was minted for. Bounded by the codec's connection-lifetime cap.

capability.description: The compact-JWS resource capability to present in the subscribe frame for this channel. Opaque to the client: never parsed, never logged, never persisted to disk (#realtime-edge-security-privacy).

channel.description: The channel this capability is bound to, echoed as the server classified it. A capability is admissible on this channel and no other.

operations.description: The operations granted, in the vocabulary's own order. Equal to the caller's held set when the request named none, and to the requested subset when it did — never wider than either.

expires_at.description: Expiry, integer seconds since the Unix epoch. The client refreshes inside a randomized window before this instant; expiry is enforced by the edge even if a refresh never arrives.

lifetime_seconds.description: Seconds this capability was minted for. Bounded by the codec's resource-lifetime cap, which is shorter than the connection cap's.

channel.description: The object-scoped mux channel this capability is for, e.g. `doc:<uuid>`. Parsed by the shared channel classifier; a static, control or unrecognized channel is refused.

operations.description: Optional narrowing. Omit to receive exactly what the caller's role on the object grants. When present it must be a non-empty, duplicate-free SUBSET of that set; a request for an operation the caller does not hold is refused, never quietly reduced.

subprotocol.description: The `cap-v1-<compact-JWS>` value to present as the WebSocket subprotocol. Restricted: it permits only the single subscribe named below. Opaque to the client (#realtime-edge-security-privacy).

expires_at.description: Expiry, integer seconds since the Unix epoch.

lifetime_seconds.description: Seconds this connection capability was minted for.

connection.description: Authority to hold one restricted socket as an anonymous reader.

capability.description: The compact-JWS resource capability for the subscribe frame. Opaque to the client (#realtime-edge-security-privacy).

channel.description: The channel this capability is bound to, echoed as the server classified it. Admissible on this channel and no other.

operations.description: The read-only operations granted, in the vocabulary's own order. Never contains `edit`.

expires_at.description: Expiry, integer seconds since the Unix epoch.

lifetime_seconds.description: Seconds this resource capability was minted for — shorter than the connection's.

resource.description: Read-only authority over exactly the published resource that was asked for.

channel.description: The object-scoped mux channel for the published resource, e.g. `doc:<uuid>` or `wiki:<uuid>`. Parsed by the shared channel classifier; a static, control or unrecognized channel is refused.

operations.description: Optional narrowing within the read-only anonymous set (`view`, `awareness`). Omit to receive both. Naming `edit` is refused — an anonymous reader is admitted for labelling, never attribution, and holds no durable authority at any link permission.

version.description: Monotonic generation count for the set. Advances when a key stops signing; a consumer holding a lower version is holding superseded material. The API refuses to publish a version below one it has already served.

kty.description: Key type. `OKP` for the Ed25519 capability keys.

kid.description: RFC 7638 JWK thumbprint of this key — what a capability's `kid` header resolves against. Derived from the key rather than configured, so it cannot disagree with it.

items.description: One verification key, in RFC 7517 JWK form.

keys.description: The active signing key first, then every retired key still inside its overlap window. A retired key is published for at least the longest capability lifetime after it stops signing, so a token minted an instant before rotation still verifies; a key withdrawn because it leaked is dropped immediately instead.

refresh_after_seconds.description: How long a consumer may go before fetching again. Advertised rather than hardcoded client-side so shortening the cadence does not need a coordinated client release.

family.description: The content-CRDT family this snapshot belongs to. `sheet` and `slide` are awareness-only families whose durable content moves through their normal REST surface, so they are refused here rather than answered with an empty snapshot.

resource_id.description: The resource id the verified capability names.

workspace_id.description: The workspace the resource lives in, taken from the verified capability. For an external collaborator holding a per-resource grant this is the OBJECT's workspace, not the caller's own.

snapshot.description: The authoritative Yjs CRDT snapshot, standard base64. `null` when the resource exists but has no CRDT lineage yet — a document created through REST and never opened collaboratively. Distinct from an absent resource, which answers 404.

snapshot_bytes.description: Decoded length of `snapshot`, or 0 when it is null. Lets a consumer size its buffer and lets an operator see snapshot growth without decoding content.

update_ref.description: `document_updates.id` — the same reference a committed envelope carries, so a consumer can tell an update it already applied from Redis apart from one it is seeing first.

update.description: One Yjs update, standard base64, applied verbatim.

window.description: The contiguous post-snapshot update window, in append order. `snapshot` is a THROTTLED checkpoint, so the durable lineage is the snapshot plus every delta appended since; a consumer applies the snapshot and then this array IN ORDER onto ONE `Y.Doc`, never a fresh one. Empty for `wiki`, which has no append-only update log and whose snapshot is therefore never a lagging checkpoint. Applying an update the snapshot already contains is a no-op — a Yjs update carries its own `(client, clock)` — so the array is bounded for memory, never fenced for correctness.

window_truncated.description: True when a bound cut the window short, so what is returned is a contiguous PREFIX of the lineage rather than all of it. Reported rather than warned about, because a consumer that cannot tell a complete lineage from a prefix will publish the prefix as current.

window_bytes.description: Decoded total length of the window's updates. Lets an operator see un-checkpointed lineage growth — the signal that a resource's checkpoint is not keeping up — without decoding content.

stream_id.description: This resource's durable sequence scope — `crdt:doc:<uuid>` or `crdt:wiki:<uuid>`, derived from the VERIFIED capability. A sequence is only meaningful inside its stream, so the position below never travels alone.

cursor_epoch.description: The number space `high_water` and `cursor` are counted in. A schema or number-space change advances it, and a cursor from an earlier space is answered with another hydrate rather than interpreted.

high_water.description: The last COMMITTED sequence when the head was read, 0 for a stream that never emitted. Read BEFORE the snapshot, so the snapshot can only contain more than this mark covers, never less — a duplicate on the caller's first catch-up is tolerated, a missing event would not be.

retention_floor.description: The highest sequence compaction has removed from this stream; 0 when nothing has been. Always strictly below `high_water + 1`, which is what makes `cursor` unconditionally resumable and one hydrate therefore enough.

cursor.description: Where the caller stands once it has applied `snapshot`, in wire form — the current epoch at `high_water`. Presenting it to catch-up resumes; it can never be answered with another hydrate instruction, because it is at or above the retention floor and at most the high-water by construction.

channel.description: The object-scoped mux channel to hydrate, e.g. `doc:<uuid>`. Parsed by the shared channel classifier; a static, control or unrecognized channel is refused. The presented capability must name exactly this family and resource id.

family.description: The awareness-only family this mirror belongs to. `doc` and `wiki` are content-CRDT families whose durable lineage is served by the hydrate route instead. A `slide` or `canvas` answer always carries a null `mirror`: legacy seeds nothing into their Y.Doc (a deck or board body matches neither seed shape), so an empty mirror is what an unchanged client already negotiates against and an invented seed would be a divergence rather than parity.

resource_id.description: The resource id the verified capability names.

workspace_id.description: The workspace the resource lives in, taken from the verified capability. For an external collaborator holding a per-resource grant this is the OBJECT's workspace, not the caller's own.

mirror.description: The transient read-only compatibility mirror as one Yjs update, standard base64 — derived on this read from the resource's authoritative JSON and never stored. `null` when there is nothing to mirror, which is never a refusal: a `sheet` with no body is a real un-authored sheet (an empty `{"sheets":[]}` body is NOT this case and derives a real mirror), and a `slide` is always null because legacy seeds no deck content. `source_bytes` still reports the body's length, so an un-authored resource and one whose family mirrors nothing stay distinguishable. Applied into a transient `Y.Doc` the consumer owns; it is not a lineage and must never be persisted.

mirror_bytes.description: Decoded length of `mirror`, or 0 when it is null. Lets a consumer size its buffer and lets an operator see mirror growth without decoding content.

source_bytes.description: Length in bytes of the authoritative JSON the mirror was derived from. Reported so an operator can see a resource approaching the source bound before a read is refused by it.

channel.description: The object-scoped mux channel to mirror, e.g. `sheet:<uuid>`. Parsed by the shared channel classifier; a static, control or unrecognized channel is refused. The presented capability must name exactly this family and resource id.

command_id.description: Echoed verbatim, so an edge can match this response to the attempt it made without holding request state.

family.description: The content-CRDT family this command committed against. `sheet` and `slide` are awareness-only families whose durable writes move through their normal REST surface; they are refused here.

resource_id.description: The resource id the verified capability names.

workspace_id.description: The workspace the resource lives in, taken from the verified capability. For an external collaborator holding a per-resource grant this is the OBJECT's workspace, not the caller's own.

snapshot_bytes.description: Decoded length of the merged lineage this command produced. Lets an operator watch snapshot growth without decoding content, and lets an edge size the buffer a subsequent hydrate will return. On a replay this is the length RECORDED at the original commit, not the resource's current length — later commands grow the lineage, and reporting today's length for an earlier command would be a different logical result.

replayed.description: False for the attempt that produced the effect, true for a retry carrying an already-committed `command_id`. Every other field is identical either way; this is the only place the wire distinguishes a fresh commit from a repaired retry.

stream_id.description: The exact stream this command's committed event was sequenced in — `crdt:doc:<uuid>` or `crdt:wiki:<uuid>`, built from the resource id as the database canonicalizes it. A sequence is only meaningful inside its stream, so it never travels alone.

cursor_epoch.description: The number space `sequence` was allocated in. A schema or number-space change advances it, and a cursor from an earlier epoch is answered with one bounded hydrate rather than interpreted in the new space.

sequence.description: The committed position inside `(stream_id, cursor_epoch)`, 1-based and contiguous. The API commits the mutation and its outbox row atomically and returns this; only then may the edge acknowledge persistence and expose the update as committed. A retry returns the ORIGINAL sequence — a second number for one logical command would burn the first and leave a permanent gap in the reader's detector.

channel.description: The object-scoped mux channel this command targets, e.g. `doc:<uuid>`. Parsed by the shared channel classifier; a static, control or unrecognized channel is refused. The presented capability must name exactly this family and resource id.

command_id.description: The edge's stable id for this BATCH, unique per logical command and REUSED verbatim on retry. The edge derives it from the batch's key and its ordered per-update ids, so re-deriving it from an unchanged payload yields the same value and a retry cannot mint a second identity for one commit. It is the durable idempotency key: the API claims it in a ledger inside the same transaction as the write, so a retry after a lost response produces one effect and returns the original result with `replayed: true`. Scoped to the workspace, so two workspaces may pick the same id independently. Reusing one id for a DIFFERENT command — another resource, another update — is refused 409 rather than answered with the first command's result.

operation.description: The durable act being commanded. One member today because this route commits exactly one: appending a CRDT update to the resource's lineage. Declared on the wire rather than implied because the API refuses a command whose declared act is not the one this route performs.

updates.description: The batch's ordered Yjs updates, each standard base64, committed as ONE transaction against the resource's lineage. Plural because the edge batches per resource for at most 25 ms or 256 KiB and sends the window as one call; a batch of one is the degenerate case, not a second spelling. Order is the sender's and is preserved in the append-only log — the merged document is order-independent (a Yjs update carries its own `(client, clock)`), but the log rows are not, and `command_id` is derived from the ordered ids. Every entry is rejected before any row is locked if it does not decode as base64 or does not apply as a Yjs update, and one bad entry refuses the whole batch: a batch is one commit, so there is no partial acceptance to report. The 256 ceiling is the API's own bound on rows per transaction (`agents/ENGINEERING.md` P16/P18) and must never fall below the edge's count trigger (`UPDATE_BATCHER.maxUpdatesPerBatch`), or valid batches would be refused.

family.description: The content-CRDT family this checkpoint advanced. `sheet` and `slide` are awareness-only families with no CRDT lineage; they are refused here.

resource_id.description: The resource id the verified capability names.

workspace_id.description: The workspace the resource lives in, taken from the verified capability. For an external collaborator holding a per-resource grant this is the OBJECT's workspace, not the caller's own.

stream_id.description: The exact stream whose checkpoint fence this advanced — `crdt:doc:<uuid>` or `crdt:wiki:<uuid>`, built from the resource id as the database canonicalizes it.

checkpoint_sequence.description: The checkpoint fence AFTER this request — the highest contiguous committed sequence the stored snapshot now provably covers. Equal to the prior fence on a no-op, raised to `covers_through_sequence` when this request advanced it. Item 2.44 prunes the buffered update window at or below this value.

advanced.description: True when this request raised the fence and merged the snapshot; false for a delayed checkpoint (coverage at or below the recorded fence) or a replay, which changed nothing.

snapshot_bytes.description: Decoded length of the resource's lineage after the merge — the current stored length on a no-op. Lets an operator watch snapshot growth without decoding content.

pruned_updates.description: Buffered `document_updates` rows this request pruned — the delivered-and-covered prefix of the delta window the snapshot has made redundant. A row is removed only when the checkpoint fence covers it AND its committed outbox event has been delivered, so a concurrent newer delta (above the fence) and a pending event's referenced bytes are never discarded. Runs on the no-op path too, so a redelivery converges the window without a new fence; zero when nothing was newly prunable, and always zero for `wiki` (full-state persistence keeps no delta log).

channel.description: The object-scoped mux channel this checkpoint targets, e.g. `doc:<uuid>`. Parsed by the shared channel classifier; a static, control or unrecognized channel is refused. The presented capability must name exactly this family and resource id.

operation.description: The durable act being commanded. One member because this route performs exactly one: advancing the resource's snapshot and its checkpoint fence. Declared on the wire rather than implied so the API refuses a request whose declared act is not the one this route performs.

snapshot.description: The edge's full resident Yjs state for this resource, standard base64. Merged onto the existing lineage (a union by `(client, clock)`, never a replacement), so a snapshot captured before a later committed delta cannot regress the stored state. Rejected before any row is locked if it does not decode as base64 or does not apply as a Yjs update.

covers_through_sequence.description: The highest CONTIGUOUS committed sequence this snapshot has absorbed — the fence. Recorded verbatim (capped below the stream head), never the current head, which is what makes a delayed checkpoint unable to cover a concurrent newer delta. Monotonic on the server: a value at or below the recorded fence is a no-op, and a value above the committed head is refused rather than clamped.

live_hydration.description: Canonical Live inbox tail and unread projection read in the same database snapshot as cursor. The edge must consume this evidence before adopting a hydrate cursor; browser rendering remains a separate REST hydration.

decision.description: `resume` carries the slice after the presented cursor. `hydrate` carries none and instructs the caller to re-establish from authoritative state first — a first connect, a legacy or superseded epoch, or a position beyond anything this stream allocated.

hydrate_reason.description: Why authoritative re-establishment was required; null on a resume. Reported apart so a rise in legacy-epoch traffic is not read as a rise in epoch bumps — the two have different operational meanings and the legacy adapter has a stated end date. `behind_retention_floor` is a third meaning again: the caller's next sequences have been compacted away, so it was away longer than the retention window rather than caught by a deploy.

stream_id.description: The exact durable stream this slice came from — `crdt:doc:<uuid>` or `crdt:wiki:<uuid>`, derived from the VERIFIED capability rather than from the request. A sequence is only meaningful inside its stream, so it never travels alone.

cursor_epoch.description: The number space this slice's sequences live in. A schema or number-space change advances it; a cursor from an earlier space is answered with a hydrate instruction rather than interpreted here.

high_water.description: The last COMMITTED sequence in this stream when the head was read, 0 for a stream that never emitted. Read BEFORE the events below, so an event committing between the two reads is returned above this mark rather than hidden beneath a mark the caller was told it reached.

retention_floor.description: The highest sequence compaction has removed from this stream; 0 when nothing has been. Reported on every answer rather than only on a behind-floor hydrate, so a long-idle subscription can watch the boundary climb toward it and re-establish before it is overtaken.

events.description: Contiguous and ascending, strictly after the presented position, bounded by `page_max_events`. Empty on a hydrate decision, and empty on a resume that was already current.

cursor.description: Where the caller stands after applying `events`, in wire form. On a hydrate decision it is where the caller will stand once it has hydrated — it must not be adopted before that.

has_more.description: More remains: the page bound filled, the slice did not reach `high_water`, or a hole stopped it. A caller drains again while this is true — unless `gap_at` is set, in which case draining cannot help.

current.description: Whether the caller may report this sequenced channel current. True only when nothing remains, which means the slice reached at least the advertised `high_water` with no hole and no page left over. Always false on a hydrate decision: the caller has applied nothing yet.

gap_at.description: The first sequence missing from the committed run, or null. Non-null is durable-state damage rather than a caller defect — the allocator serializes writers per stream, so a hole has no sanctioned producer until compaction records a stream floor. The slice stops BEFORE it, because a receiver advances its checkpoint only after applying an event and a checkpoint moved past a hole loses that event permanently.

page_max_events.description: The bound this slice was taken under, reported rather than implied so a caller can tell a full page from a short one without knowing the server's knob.

event_id.description: The event's globally unique id — the receiver's de-duplication key. Delivery is at-least-once: the same event can arrive from Redis fan-out and from this slice, and applying it twice must be a no-op.

sequence.description: The committed position inside `(stream_id, cursor_epoch)`. Contiguous with its neighbours in this slice by construction — the slice stops at the first missing sequence rather than skipping it.

producer_kind.description: Which class of producer emitted the event.

producer_id.description: The producer's workspace-prefixed idempotency key. Stable across a retry of one logical emission, which is what makes one command yield one event.

envelope_version.description: Schema version of `envelope`. Readable without parsing the envelope, so a consumer can refuse an unknown version rather than mis-read a known-looking one.

envelope.description: The minimum versioned delivery envelope: what changed and where, never the durable content itself. Y.Doc content stays in the API-owned database under its own retention.

created_at.description: Commit time, ISO 8601. Ordering is by `sequence`, never by this.

channel.description: The mux channel to catch up: an object-scoped `doc:<uuid>`/`wiki:<uuid>`, or the static `live` recipient channel. Parsed by the shared channel classifier; a control, unrecognized, relay-only (`presence`/`sync`) or not-yet-served (`chat`/`mail`) channel is refused. For an object channel the presented capability must name exactly this family and resource id; for `live` it is the connection capability, whose subject is the recipient. Either way the durable stream is derived from that capability rather than from this field.

cursor.description: The caller's last applied position, `<stream-id>@<epoch>.<sequence>`. Absent or null means it holds none — a first connect, answered with `decision: "hydrate"` rather than with the whole history. A cursor from a supported legacy or superseded number space is likewise answered with a hydrate instruction and the current-space position, never reinterpreted in the new space.

model.description: Active LLM model identifier (e.g. `gpt-5.4-mini`). Surfaced in the assistant header so users see what is answering them.

tool_name.description: Assistant tool that produced the entry (e.g. `create_task`).

resource_type.description: Resource the tool created/modified (e.g. `task`, `document`). Null for tool calls without a resource (rare).

path.description: Router path the UI should navigate to on click (e.g. `/tasks`, `/docs/abc`). Null when the tool has no canonical destination.

reasoning.description: Stored reasoning summary of the assistant turn, capped at 32,000 chars head-keep with a visible `...[truncated N chars]` marker. Owner-only — never present on the public share projection.

PlanTier.description: Workspace billing tier. `free` is the default; `pro` is the paid Stripe plan.

TopUpPack.description: Top-up pack size — small (500 actions / $5), medium (2,500 / $20), large (10,000 / $50).

ActionsLedgerSource.description: Caller class — drives the metering dispatch matrix.

token.description: Single-use verification token from the click-through link.

snippet.description: Excerpt around the first body match; empty when the title matched.

score.description: Relevance score (higher = better). Ordering only — never a stable value.

updated_at.description: ISO-8601 of the row's own recency axis — what `sort: "recent"` orders on and what a row renders as "2h ago".

avatar_url.description: Profile photo URL on People results; null when the person has none.

counts.description: Per-module match total BEFORE the per-module cap, capped at 500 (a hotter term reads 500+). Keyed by module; a module that returned no row carries no key.

preview.description: Per-module preview shape (see PRODUCT.md hover card spec).

email.description: Recipient email (empty for generic links).

role.description: Granted role (`admin` or `member`).

token.description: Invite token — embedded in the accept link sent via email.

invite_url.description: Pre-built accept URL — present for generic invite links so the caller can copy/paste without rebuilding it.

success.description: The invitation continuation cookie was set. No access has been accepted.

email.description: Email the invite was addressed to (empty for generic links).

role.description: Role the recipient will receive on accept.

inviter_name.description: Display name of the user who created the invite. Falls back to `A teammate` when the inviter row can't be resolved.

invite_type.description: What accepting produces. `external_grant` binds a per-resource grant to one identity the accepter already owns and writes no `users` row here; every other value is an arrival into the workspace. The accept page cannot tell the two apart from the other fields — both carry a workspace and a role — so the outcome has to be stated.

resource_path.description: In-app route this grant opens. Built server-side because `resource_type` cannot reach it: `document` covers docs, sheets and slides, which live on three routes.

resources.description: Every resource an `external_grant` grants, oldest first. Legacy invitations can contain several resources; new document invitations each describe one share. Empty on a membership invite, which grants no single resource. `resource_role` is the share role on that resource, never the workspace `role` above.

destination.description: Canonical accepted resource route, derived by the server.

token.description: Freshly-issued JWT — replace any prior credential with this one to begin acting in the target workspace.

workspace_email.description: Per-workspace email (e.g. `alice@acme.ambi.cc`). Null until the workspace email is provisioned.

workspace_added.description: True when an EXISTING user was added to a new workspace; absent / false on first registration via invite.

workspaces.description: All workspaces the user now belongs to after accepting (sorted in the order returned by the service).

display_name.description: Display name to set on a newly-created account. Membership invites only — required when accepting one as a brand-new user, ignored when an authenticated user accepts a second-workspace invite, and never honored on an `external_grant`, which refuses an unauthenticated accept outright.

password.description: Password for the new account. Membership invites only, on the same terms as `display_name` above.

accept_as_workspace_id.description: `external_grant` only: which of the accepter's own identities the grant binds to, named by the workspace that identity lives in. Sent only when the accepter chose — an account holding one identity has nothing to choose and omits it. Resolved against the accepting account's own rows, so it can never name another account's identity.

expected_invite_id.description: Reject if another tab replaced the invitation context.

success.description: True — the invite token is invalidated and can no longer be accepted.

completed.description: Tasks completed in the trailing window.

updated.description: Tasks with updates in the trailing window.

opened.description: Tasks newly opened in the trailing window.

HomeVelocityCounts.description: Current-window count minus the prior window of the same length (may be negative).

actor_type.description: Coworker rows carry the 'AI' badge on the surface; humans do not.

counts_by_module.description: Top modules the actor touched in the window, capped server-side.

last_at.description: ISO-8601 timestamp of the actor's most recent activity in the window.

digest.description: Actor-aggregated activity, visibility-gated per viewer, most-recent first.

published_at.description: ISO 8601 date (no time) the entry was published.

version.description: Semver version this entry corresponds to. Bumped when any breaking change lands.

summary.description: Body of the entry — what changed, why, and any caveats agents need to know.

breaking.description: True if the change removes/renames a path/field, can silently 200 with wrong data, or shifts auth/permissions.

decision_id.description: Matching row in `agents/DECISIONS.md` (e.g. `D107`). Null if no formal decision was recorded.

migration.description: Short migration note describing what callers must do. Null if no action required. Always present when `breaking` is true.

areas.description: Module tags the entry applies to (e.g. `Identity`, `Mail`).

has_more.description: Pagination flag — always false because the changelog is a static list, not a paginated query.

success.description: `true` on the 200 path. The route returns 200 only once the task exists — there is no receipt without a record.

feedback_id.description: The receipt — the id of the task that stores the submission. Pass it to `GET /api/feedback/{id}` to read the status back.

error.description: Stable string code. `Invalid input` for body-shape failures, `Invalid request body` for non-JSON, `Feedback reporting not available` when the intake is not configured (503 — surfaced via raw Response since 503 is outside the contract `ErrorCode` enum), `Feedback not found` on the reads.

details.description: Zod issue array on validation failures — for diagnostic UIs that want field-level error rendering.

feedback_id.description: A throwaway id on the 400 paths so an aborted submission still has a support handle; no task exists for it.

FeedbackStatus.description: The submitter-facing status, derived on every read from the task's system status: `filed` (todo), `accepted` (in progress or blocked), `declined` (cancelled or trashed), `shipped` (done).

FeedbackPriority.description: Triage priority as the submitter set it — p0 critical, p1 high, p2 medium, p3 low. Optional on submit; an omitted priority is stored as `low`.

feedback_id.description: The receipt — the id of the task that stores the submission.

title.description: The task title: the submitter's, or the generated one.

priority.description: The task's current priority, mapped back to the wire code.

task_key.description: The task's human-readable key in Ambiguous's workspace, e.g. `TASK-6768` — a support handle.

FeedbackItem.description: The public projection of one submission. Nothing else on the task is exposed.

authorization_servers.description: Authorization server URLs that issue tokens for this resource. The server itself is the only entry.

bearer_methods_supported.description: Where the bearer token is accepted — only `header` (Authorization).

access_token.description: Long-lived API key (`ak_*`) — use as a Bearer token.

workspace_email.description: Computed in-workspace address (`<username>@<default-workspace-domain>`). A verified custom domain is used only after an Admin selects it as the workspace default.

enabled_skills.description: Skills this coworker is scoped to. Null = full workspace skill set.

avatar_url.description: The agent's avatar image. Null when none is set.

workspace_email.description: Computed in-workspace address (`<username>@<default-workspace-domain>`). A verified custom domain is used only after an Admin selects it as the workspace default.

kind.description: `coworker` runs the first-party engine; `agent` is a third-party identity.

manager.description: The human accountable for this agent. Null when unassigned.

coworker_config_id.description: The coworker configuration id. Null for a third-party agent.

last_active_at.description: The later of the agent's last activity and its newest API-key use. Null when never active.

pending_approvals.description: Email submissions to or from this agent awaiting a decision the caller may see. Review them with `GET /api/mail/approvals?agent_id=`.

AgentEmailAccessScope.description: `workspace` (Workspace members only) — send and receive within this workspace; an external send awaits human approval, and external incoming mail is bounced to its sender and held for a human to admit. `anyone` (Anyone on the internet) — send and receive with people inside and outside this workspace.

dms.description: Hear direct messages sent to this agent.

tasks_assigned.description: Hear tasks assigned to this agent.

docs_shared.description: Hear docs/wiki shared with this agent.

emails.description: Hear emails delivered to this agent's mailbox.

thread_replies.description: Hear replies in threads this agent authored, replied in, or was mentioned in.

watched_channel_ids.description: Channel ids whose messages this agent hears (must be a member).

keywords.description: Keywords that, when matched in an accessible message, this agent hears.

connected.description: A live agent connection is currently registered for this agent.

raw_key.description: The plaintext key. Returned once — the server sends Cache-Control: no-store.
The new plaintext key. Returned once — the server sends Cache-Control: no-store.

old_key_expires_at.description: ISO timestamp when the previous key stops authenticating, 24 hours after rotation.

workspace_email.description: Computed in-workspace address (`<username>@<default-workspace-domain>`). A verified custom domain is used only after an Admin selects it as the workspace default.

agent_kind.description: `coworker` runs the first-party engine; `agent` is a third-party identity.

manager.description: The human who reviews this agent's held emails. Null when unassigned.

can_manage.description: Whether the CALLING principal may change the scope. An agent reading its own scope gets false — only a human manager or human admin/owner may write it.

agent_kind.description: `coworker` runs the first-party engine; `agent` is a third-party identity.

agent_optimizer_enabled.description: Whether each consequential (non-read-only) call this agent makes is reviewed before it runs. Off by default.

manager.description: The human accountable for this agent. Null when unassigned.

agent_optimizer_enabled.description: Turn the optimizer on (`true`) or off (`false`) for this agent.

reason.description: The rubric's fail reasons on `fail`, the agent's own reason on `skipped`, the failure on `error`; null on `pass`.

rubric.description: Per-dimension scores and fail reasons as parsed; null unless the call was reviewed.

request.description: The operation input exactly as the reviewer was sent it (`params`, `query`, `body`), secrets redacted.

actions_charged.description: Actions this decision cost the workspace: 1 for a completed review (`pass` or `fail`), 0 otherwise.

AgentOptimizerVerdict.description: `pass` — reviewed, the call ran. `fail` — reviewed, the call was refused. `skipped` — the agent bypassed the review with a reason, the call ran. `error` — the review could not complete, the call ran unreviewed and the action was refunded.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` to read the next page; null on the last page.

TeamVisibility.description: `public` = listed and joinable. `private` = members + admins only.

TeamJoinPolicy.description: How non-members can join. `open` = self-serve. `request` = request-to-join (creates a `TeamJoinRequest`). `invite` = invite required.

TeamPostingPolicy.description: Who may post to the team's email address. `open` = any sender. `members_only` = workspace members. `admins_only` = team admins.

TeamMemberRole.description: Role within one team. Workspace role is separate.

workspace_email.description: Computed in-workspace address (`<username>@<default-workspace-domain>`). A verified custom domain is used only after an Admin selects it as the workspace default.
Computed in-workspace address (`<username>@<default-workspace-domain>`). A verified custom domain is used only after an Admin selects it as the workspace default.
Computed in-workspace address (`<username>@<default-workspace-domain>`). A verified custom domain is used only after an Admin selects it as the workspace default.

error.description: invalid_report_reference | report_not_found | invalid_report_spec — set instead of `result` when the tile could not be executed.

source.description: Which read served this page. Set by `analytics_users_list` only.

error.description: Set by `analytics_users_aggregates` when the materialized view is missing or unpopulated; the page is empty rather than an error status.

id.description: The resource's id, not the grant's.

title.description: The resource's current title — a file's name, a calendar's name.

role.description: The role the caller holds. Where two grants reach one resource (named AND through a team, or two identities of one account) this is the STRONGER — the one that decides access.

shared_by.description: Who wrote the grant. `null` where the grant predates the recorded sharer.

shared_at.description: When the grant was written — the GRANT's timestamp, never the resource's `updated_at`, which moves whenever anyone edits it. The list is ordered on this, newest first.

SharedResourceType.description: Which Pat8 surface the row is on. `document` covers docs, sheets and slides — they are one table and one permission model.

SharedVia.description: `direct` — a named grant on an identity in the resource's own workspace. `team` — a grant on a team the caller resolves through, nesting included. `external` — a named grant held by an identity in ANOTHER workspace.

SharedWithMeResponse.description: Cursor-paginated, newest share first. Workspace-tier access is NOT a share and is absent: an Everyone-team row grants standing authority to every member (`agents/modules/TEAMS.md` P6), so listing it would put every workspace-visible resource in every member's list.

username.description: The agent's workspace email local-part, derived from the name.

workspace_email.description: The agent's inbound address inside this workspace's domain.

api_key.description: The agent's API key (`ak_…`). **Returned exactly once, here** — never retrievable again; rotate the key to get a new one.

harness.description: Echo of the harness the journey carried, so the completion screen can open the right connect instructions without a second read.

declined.description: Always true on a 200 — the prompt is silenced. A literal rather than a boolean because there is no `false` to answer with: a call that found nothing left to decline is a 409, not a successful non-decline.

acknowledged.description: Always true on a 200 — the step is closed. A literal for the same reason the decline's is: a call that found no provisioned agent to acknowledge is a 409, not a successful non-acknowledgement.

raw_key.description: Plaintext API key. Only returned at create and rotate time.

AutomationRunStatus.description: Terminal status when the dispatch returns. `suspended` means a delay or until-event node parked the run; the scheduler will resume it asynchronously and the final status will appear on `GET /api/automations/runs/:runId` (Rock 5 item 28).

output.description: Full-fidelity output of the terminal node for synchronous workflow invocation. Present on `automations_invoke` so a parent workflow receives the child workflow's result.

status_url.description: Poll this path with the same workspace credential until the run reaches a terminal status.

AutomationRunInput.description: Trigger payload for a manual run. Forwarded verbatim to the manualTrigger node. Shape is workflow-author-defined; downstream nodes reference fields via `{var: "<NodeName>.field"}` JSONLogic expressions.

AutomationVisibility.description: Workflow visibility. `private` (default): only the owner + `shared_with` viewers can see it. `workspace`: every member of the workspace can read it (edit still gated by `shared_with`). `public_link` is reserved for future read-only sharing and currently reads exactly like `private`: `canReadAutomation` grants workspace-wide read only for `workspace`.

id.description: Node id, unique within the workflow.

name.description: Human-readable node name; doubles as the JSONLogic var prefix.

type.description: Node primitive (`manualTrigger`, `webhook`, `filter`, `branch`, `delay`, `loop`, `code`, …) or registry-action type (`task.create`, `email.send`, …).

position.description: Canvas position [x, y]. Optional; defaults to [0, 0].

parameters.description: Per-node configuration. Shape is node-type-specific.

connections.description: Adjacency map keyed by node `name` (n8n convention). Values describe outgoing edges per port.

AutomationWorkflow.description: Workflow JSONB. n8n-shaped: `nodes` array + `connections` adjacency keyed by node name. Inner shape is enforced by the dispatcher, not at the API layer.

node_id.description: Id of the unrecognized workflow node.

node_name.description: Human-readable name of the unrecognized workflow node.

type.description: Unrecognized node type preserved on the workflow.

did_you_mean.description: Likely registered operationIds or n8n alias keys, nearest first.

owner_workspace_email.description: Computed in-workspace address (`<username>@<default-workspace-domain>`). A verified custom domain is used only after an Admin selects it as the workspace default.

warnings.description: Advisory warnings for unrecognized node types. Omitted when none are found.

AutomationSaveResponse.description: A saved workflow with optional advisory node-type warnings.

description.description: Optional long-form description; surfaced in the UI catalog.

allOf.description: Initial workflow JSONB. `workflow_version` starts at 1; subsequent PATCHes write `automation_workflow_versions` rows + bump the version.

active.description: Whether the workflow is enabled to fire on triggers. Defaults to `false` (draft) on create — call POST `/:id/enable` to activate (item 26).

allOf.description: Defaults to `private`.

tags.description: Free-form tag strings; usable as a list-filter (`?tag=foo`).

owner_workspace_email.description: Computed in-workspace address (`<username>@<default-workspace-domain>`). A verified custom domain is used only after an Admin selects it as the workspace default.

Automation.description: A workflow row. `workflow_version` is the live cursor; immutable snapshots live in `automation_workflow_versions`. Returned by every CRUD route.

total.description: Count of rows in this page.

has_more.description: True if a subsequent page exists. Set when the underlying query returned `limit + 1` hint rows.

type.description: Stable identifier used in `workflow.nodes[].type`. Primitives are hand-coded names (`webhook`, `filter`, `delay`); actions are the underlying route's `operationId` verbatim (e.g., `create_task`, `crm_deal_stage_move`, `automations_invoke`).

label.description: Human-readable label rendered in the UI palette. Display only — never used as identity. For primitives this is hand-coded; for actions it's derived mechanically from the operationId + tag via `formatActionLabel()` (e.g., `tasks_create` + `Tasks` → 'Create task').

module.description: Group key used for the palette tree. For primitives, equals the literal type string (`webhook`, `filter`, etc.). For actions, the lowercased OpenAPI tag (e.g., `tasks` for routes tagged `Tasks`).

description.description: One-line description of what the node does. Primitives are documented inline; action descriptions come from the route's OpenAPI `description` field, truncated at 200 chars.

deferred.description: True when the node is registered but not yet implemented — the engine recognizes the type but emits `{status: 'failed', error: '<type> deferred to v1.1'}`. Set on no node type at HEAD (the `code` primitive now executes in the WASM isolate).

n8n_aliases.description: Inbound n8n-nodes-base type strings that route to this node-type via the alias table (Pat4). Surfaced by the catalog so the UI palette can label imported workflows. Populated by Rock 7 item 36 once the alias table is loaded; absent until then.

NodeTypeCategory.description: `trigger` is one of the five trigger primitives (webhook / scheduleTrigger / manualTrigger / event / email); `control` is one of the five DAG-control primitives (filter / branch / delay / loop / code); `action` is a registry-derived node that wraps an HTTP route with `x-tool.expose: ['automations']`.

primitives.description: The ten hand-coded primitives, ordered triggers first (webhook, scheduleTrigger, manualTrigger, event, email) then DAG control (filter, branch, delay, loop, code).

actions.description: Registry-derived actions, sorted by `type`. Empty until at least one route is registered with `x-tool.expose: ['automations']`. Adding a new action route makes the action appear here on next server boot — no automations-module code changes needed (Pat2).

NodeTypeListResponse.description: Unified node-type catalog. UI palette reads this live to render the node-picker tree. Per Pat2 the palette groups action entries by their `module` field (lowercased OpenAPI tag).

id.description: Stable handle id used by edges as the `sourceHandle`.

label.description: Human-readable label rendered next to the port in the canvas.

NodeOutput.description: One declared output port on a node type. Multi-output primitives (currently only `branch`) ship at least the `default` fallthrough port; runtime fan-out beyond the static list is signalled by `outputs_from_parameters`.

operation_id.description: For actions, equals `type` — the route's operationId is the identity (e.g., `create_task`). NULL for primitives — they aren't backed by a registered route. Kept as a separate field so primitive-vs-action discrimination is one-shot (`operation_id === null` ⇒ primitive).

http_method.description: HTTP method of the underlying route for actions. NULL for primitives.

http_path.description: Path template of the underlying route for actions, e.g., `/api/tasks` or `/api/automations/{id}/run`. NULL for primitives.

input_schema.description: JSON Schema (draft-07-ish, converted from zod) describing valid `node.parameters` shape for this type. For actions, this is the route's request body schema. For primitives, this is the hand-coded parameter shape (e.g., the filter's `{predicate: <JSONLogic>}` or the delay's `{wakeAt | duration_ms}`). NULL when no schema is available — the dispatcher will accept any parameters but the UI cannot render a typed form.

outputs.description: Static output ports a node-type declares at design time. Populated for primitives that fan out at runtime — currently `branch` ships `[{id:'default', label:'Default'}]` as the no-match fallthrough. Absent for single-output primitives and actions, where the implicit single `main` output is the contract.

outputs_from_parameters.description: Runtime-derived output hint. When set, consumers expand outputs beyond the static `outputs` list by walking `node.parameters.<source>`. Today only `{ source: 'cases' }` is emitted, by `branch` — `parameters.cases[].then` names the per-case output ports.

NodeTypeDetail.description: Full record for a single node type, including the parameter input schema. Returned by `GET /api/automations/node-types/:type`.

clean.description: Count of `={{ ... }}` parameter expressions that translated cleanly to JSONLogic (Tier A).

code_fallback.description: Count of expressions that fell back to a `code` node body (Tier B). The `code` primitive executes that body in the WASM isolate, so a Tier-B fallback runs rather than failing.

unsupported.description: Count of expressions flagged as unsupported (Tier C — banned identifiers like `$workflow`, `process`, `require`, etc.). The user must rewrite these by hand before enabling.

AutomationImportSummary.description: Aggregate counts of expression-translation outcomes across the imported workflow.

AutomationImportNodeReview.description: Per-node compatibility review. It contains identifiers and compatibility metadata, never node parameters, expressions, credentials, payloads, or binary data.

nodeName.description: Display name of the imported node.

n8nType.description: Original `node.type` string from the imported file (e.g., `n8n-nodes-base.slack`).

suggestion.description: Curated user-facing suggestion for replacing the unsupported node. Falls through to a generic suggestion when no curated copy exists for the type.

parameter.description: Dotted path to the `parameters.*` field that contained the banned-identifier expression.

originalJs.description: Verbatim original `={{ ... }}` expression body, preserved for the review pane.

reason.description: Human-readable reason the expression was flagged unsupported (e.g., `banned identifier: $workflow`).

parameter.description: Dotted path to the `parameters.*` field that contained the non-trivial JS expression.

originalJs.description: Verbatim original `={{ ... }}` expression body. Will be wrapped in a `code` node body once the `code` primitive ships in v1.1.

automation_id.description: `automations.id` of the freshly-inserted draft row (always created with `active=false`).

node_reviews.description: Every imported node classified as supported, mapping-required, or unsupported.

unsupported_nodes.description: Nodes whose type or operation configuration has no native execution equivalent. The dispatcher fails loudly when these are reached at runtime — operators see them in the review pane and replace or reconfigure them before enabling.

unsupported_expressions.description: Tier-C expressions (banned identifiers) — must be rewritten by hand.

tier_b_pending.description: Tier-B expressions surfaced for review because they translated to a `code` node body rather than to JSONLogic. Stored verbatim on the workflow JSONB so they round-trip back to n8n via `automations_export?format=n8n`.

AutomationImportResponse.description: Body of a successful `POST /api/automations/import?source=n8n` response. Carries the import-review pane data: which expressions translated cleanly, which fell back to `code`, which were flagged unsupported.

file.description: The n8n workflow JSON file to import (multipart `file` field).

values.description: The resolved values, returned verbatim so downstream nodes can reference them via `{var: "<NodeName>.values.<key>"}` JSONLogic expressions.

AutomationHttpRequestResponse.description: Outbound response status, headers, and content-type-aware body for downstream nodes.

AutomationTriggerSource.description: Origin of a workflow run. `manual` is the operator-initiated run from /api/automations/:id/run. `event` / `webhook` / `schedule` / `email` are the four production trigger primitives. `test` is the dry-run path (Rock 5 item 27).

allOf.description: Terminal status of an automation run. `success` is the happy path; `filtered` means a trigger or filter rejected the payload before any action ran; `failed` carries an error message; `suspended` is a delay/until_event mid-run park awaiting scheduler resume; `cancelled` is operator-initiated; `depth_exceeded` short-circuits when nested workflows exceed the spec P16 cap of 3.

workflow_version_at_dispatch.description: `automations.workflow_version` snapshot at dispatch time. Re-running a historic run uses this version's snapshot from `automation_workflow_versions` instead of the current `workflow`.

step_outputs.description: Per-node outputs (truncated to 4 KB per node before persist).

meta.description: Run-metadata envelope. v1 keys: `parentRunId` (set by retry), `cancelledBy` + `cancelledAt` (set by cancel).

finished_at.description: NULL while suspended/running; set on terminal status.

allOf.description: The cancelled run row, with `meta.cancelledBy`/`meta.cancelledAt` recorded and any matching scheduler row consumed.
The newly dispatched retry run. Lineage to the parent is recorded on `meta.parentRunId`.
The workflow with its webhook node's `parameters.ingestKeyHash` updated.

ingest_key.description: The newly generated plaintext ingest key. Returned exactly ONCE, never persisted in plaintext. Use it to update Sentry / Stripe / GitHub webhook URLs that point at this workflow.

webhook_url.description: The full webhook URL with the new key — convenience for copy-paste into external sender configs. Path is `/api/automations/webhook/:ingestKey`; the host is omitted so the caller resolves it against their environment.

total.description: Count of rows in this page.

has_more.description: True if a subsequent page exists. Set when the underlying query returned `limit + 1` hint rows.

hour.description: UTC hour bucket (`date_trunc('hour', started_at)`) as ISO 8601.

count.description: Run count for this hour. Empty hours are absent from the array.

version.description: Monotonically-increasing version number. v1 is seeded on create; every subsequent PATCH-with-workflow-change appends a new row at the next integer.

allOf.description: Immutable snapshot of the workflow JSONB at this version — the exact bytes that were stored on `automations.workflow` at the time. Restore copies this back verbatim.

edited_by.description: User who created this version row. May be NULL if the user has been removed (FK is ON DELETE SET NULL — history rows survive editor removal for audit-trail integrity).

edit_summary.description: Optional human note recorded on the version row when the workflow changed. NULL on rows where the editor didn't supply a summary.

AutomationWorkflowVersion.description: An immutable workflow snapshot. Append-only; never mutated or deleted (apart from cascade on parent automation delete).

total.description: Count of rows in this page.

has_more.description: True if a subsequent page exists. Set when the underlying query returned `limit + 1` hint rows.

allOf.description: The parent workflow with `workflow` byte-restored from the historical version and `workflow_version` bumped to the new top-of-history value.

The newly-appended version row carrying the byte-identical snapshot. Its `version` number is the new top-of-history (NOT the source version's number) — restore is non-destructive and preserves the prior history.

format.description: Which document this body carries. `native` is the workflow JSONB verbatim; `n8n` is the translated n8n-shaped document — check `X-Automations-Lossy-Translation` for round-trip fidelity.

workflow_version.description: `automations.workflow_version` at export time. Recorded so the consumer can detect drift when re-importing. Present on both formats.

allOf.description: The workflow document. On `format=native` these are the raw JSONB bytes of `Automation.workflow` — no translation, no truncation. On `format=n8n` the nodes carry reversed `={{ ... }}` parameters.

exported_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the export. Useful for change-tracking.

AutomationExportNativeResponse.description: Body of a successful `GET /api/automations/:id/export` response, either format. Native-format export carries the workflow JSONB verbatim — re-importing produces a byte-identical row.

workspace_email.description: Computed in-workspace address (`<username>@<default-workspace-domain>`). A verified custom domain is used only after an Admin selects it as the workspace default.

allOf.description: If provided, the engine writes a new row to `automation_workflow_versions` AND increments `automations.workflow_version` per spec P21.

active.description: Direct toggle. The dedicated `_enable`/`_disable` lifecycle routes (item 26) are sugar over this same field.

edit_summary.description: Optional human note recorded on the version row when the `workflow` field changes.

AutomationUpdateInput.description: Partial update. Only fields explicitly present in the body are written; omitted fields keep their prior value. If `workflow` is included, a new immutable version row is created.

ips.description: CIDR ranges (IPv4 + IPv6) the workspace's outbound HTTP traffic may originate from. Best-effort — Cloud Run egress is not strictly static, so allowlist consumers should periodically re-fetch this list.

region.description: GCP region the runtime currently deploys to. Today: `us-west1`. v1.1 may add additional regions; the response will list every active region's egress range.

source.description: Upstream source the IP list is derived from. Today: `https://www.gstatic.com/ipranges/cloud.json` filtered to the active region. Consumers can fetch this URL directly for the freshest possible list.

note.description: Disclaimer about the best-effort nature of the list. v1 publishes a representative subset of the GCP us-west1 ranges; v1.1 adds a static-egress NAT and tightens the disclaimer.

last_verified.description: ISO 8601 date the published list was last manually verified against the upstream source. Stale dates are a signal to re-fetch upstream rather than trust this response.

AutomationsWellKnownIpsResponse.description: Public response of `GET /.well-known/automations-ips`. No auth required — corporate firewalls fetch this without credentials to populate their allowlists for inbound webhook senders that Ambiguous routes through (Slack, Sentry, etc.).

retention_days.description: null means indefinite retention — no document is ever purge-eligible.

status.description: The terminal status the document was queued in — completed, voided, or expired.

purge_queued_at.description: When the retention period elapsed and the document entered the queue.

purge_after.description: When the sealed PDF is deleted. Restorable until this instant (LEGAL.md L8).

retention_days.description: This document's override. null defers to the workspace period.

workspace_retention_days.description: The workspace period this override supersedes.

purge_eligible_at.description: When this document enters the purge queue. null means indefinite — it is not terminal, or no period resolves.

valid.description: Always `true` on 200. Wrong-password attempts return 401, never `valid: false`.

type.description: Document family (`doc`, `sheet`, `slide`).

content.description: Authoring format for the document (ProseMirror JSON for docs/wiki, JSON for sheets/slides). Shape varies by `type`.

display_name.description: Display name of the resource owner.

post.description: Dry-run a workflow against a caller-supplied payload. Action nodes (`create_task`, `send_email`, `chat_assistant`, …) are stubbed: they return success with empty outputs WITHOUT invoking the real handler, so authors can verify filters / branches / expressions without producing real-world side effects. The payload binds to the workflow's entry node (any node with no incoming edges — `manualTrigger`, `webhook`, `scheduleTrigger`, `event`, `email`, or any other root); trigger TYPE is metadata for automatic invocation only and does not gate test dispatch. The optional `pinData` map keys node NAMES to output values that override evaluation entirely — useful for seeding realistic upstream shapes when only part of the DAG is being tested. Test runs are recorded with `trigger_source='test'` (filtered out of the default run-history list). Test mode bypasses the `active` flag so disabled drafts can be tested. (Spec Pat11.)

post.description: Import a workflow from a third-party tool. `?source=n8n` (the only supported source for v1) accepts an n8n workflow JSON document as `multipart/form-data` with a `file` field. The handler walks every node, normalizes each `node.type` via the n8n alias table (audit §12.2.7), and runs the three-tier expression translator (audit §12.3.2) against every `={{ ... }}` parameter. The translated workflow is stored verbatim — original n8n type strings are kept on disk so `automations_export?format=n8n` round-trips cleanly; the dispatcher normalizes via `resolveNodeType()` at runtime. The response is the import-review pane: counts of clean / Tier-B-`code`-fallback / Tier-C-unsupported expressions, the list of unsupported nodes or operation configurations, and the detail rows backing each count. The created row is always `active=false` — the user reviews unsupported nodes and Tier-B fallbacks before enabling.

post.description: Dispatch a child workflow with depth-incremented envelope. Used by the `automations_invoke` action node (wired into `evaluateNode` so workflows can call other workflows).
